parsed_response.reasoning: In GoogleCalendarService deleteEvent, the diff changes the fallback to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`, evaluated only when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. In that branch `externalCalendarId` is undefined/null, so the find predicate compares each entry's externalId to undefined and effectively never matches a real calendar, yielding undefined where the old code returned `destinationCalendar?.externalId`. The same tautological pattern appears in updateEvent. This is a real regression introduced by the diff: bookings whose reference lacks externalCalendarId will pass an undefined calendarId to calendar.events.delete/update instead of the destination calendar's externalId. The exact downstream failure (event never deleted) depends on Google API behavior not shown in the diff, but the broken fallback mechanism is verifiable from the diff itself.

judged_text: deleteEvent's calendarId fallback (event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId) is evaluated only when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it matches entries whose externalId === undefined and yields undefined instead of the old destinationCalendar?.externalId. Cancelling a booking whose reference lacks externalCalendarId calls calendar.events.delete with an undefined calendarId; the remote calendar event is never deleted and the orphaned Google Meet/event entry stays on the organizer's calendar.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` changed the fallback from `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. If `externalCalendarId` is `undefined/null` (e.g., older booking references without `externalCalendarId`, as seen in cancellation flow passing `externalCalendarId` through), the `.find(...)` compares against `undefined` and typically returns `undefined`, so the service no longer targets the actual destination calendar externalId. This can cause updates/deletes to be issued against the wrong calendar (likely default/primary) and fail to remove the real event, leaving an orphaned entry.
